# 16S Primer Panel — Adversarial Verification

**Verdict: All 11 primer *sequences* are correct (verified against literature, IUPAC codes valid). The CODE in `/home/freiburger/Documents/prFBA/insilico_pcr.py` is internally consistent and computes revcomps at runtime, so it will extract correctly. BUT there is one real biological mislabel (V6-V8) and two typos in the human-readable `notes` revcomp strings. Three issues total, ranked below.**

Authoritative E. coli hypervariable spans used (Brosius 1978 numbering): V1 69-99, V2 137-242, V3 433-497, V4 576-682, V5 822-879, **V6 986-1043**, **V7 1117-1173**, V8 1243-1294, V9 1435-1465.

## Issue 1 (SERIOUS — mislabeled region): "V6-V8" actually amplifies V7-V9

1100F (`YAACGAGCGCAACCC`, E. coli ~1100-1114) is documented in the literature as a **V7F** primer (position 1099-1114). Its 3' end sits at ~1114, but **V6 ends at 1043** — V6 is entirely 5' (upstream) of the forward primer and physically cannot be in the amplicon. The 1100F/1492R amplicon covers **V7, V8, V9** (computed: fwd-3'=1114, rev-5'=1492 → captures V7/V8/V9).

Consequence: the "V6-V8" entry and the "V7-V9" entry use **identical primers** (1100F/1492R) and produce the **identical amplicon (V7-V9)**. They are biologically redundant; the "V6-V8" label is simply wrong. The panel's own note even concedes "Same primer geometry as V6-V8 ... this amplicon spans V7-V9," which is self-contradictory with the V6-V8 name.

Fix options:
- **(a) Rename** the "V6-V8" entry to "V7-V9" and drop the redundant duplicate (recommended — they extract the same bases). In code: `REGION_PANEL[7]` ("V6-V8", lines 128-134) and `REGION_PANEL[8]` ("V7-V9", lines 135-141) are byte-identical except `name`/`priority`; collapse to one.
- **(b) If V6 genuinely needs covering**, change the forward primer to one 5' of V6, e.g. **926F** (`AAACTYAAAKGAATTGRCGG`, ~E.coli 907-926, revcomp of 926R) or **967F**/**1062F**-class. 1100F cannot bound V6 under any trimming.

## Issue 2 (TYPO in notes only — code unaffected): 926R revcomp in notes

Notes for V4-V5 give the 926R sense-strand revcomp as `AAACTYAAARRAATTGRCGG`. The **M** (A/C) in `CCGYCAATTYMTTTRAGTTT` revcomps to **K** (G/T), not R. Correct = `AAACTYAAA**K**RAATTGRCGG`. The code is right (`make_extractor` recomputes via `revcomp()` at runtime; the docstring on line 146 correctly shows `[GT]`=K), so extraction is unaffected — only the prose note is wrong.

## Issue 3 (TYPO in notes only — code unaffected): 1492R revcomp in notes

Notes (both Full-length and V6-V8 entries) give the 1492R sense revcomp as `AAGTCGTAACAARGTARCCGTA`. The base preceding that position is a plain G (not degenerate), so it revcomps to plain C→G. Correct = `AAGTCGTAACAA**G**GTARCCGTA` (only one R, from the Y). The panel inserted a spurious extra R. Code unaffected (runtime revcomp).

## Items checked and CONFIRMED CORRECT

- **515F-Parada** `GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA` + **926R-Quince/Parada** `CCGYCAATTYMTTTRAGTTT` (study anchor) — matches code `FWD_515F`/`REVC_926R` exactly, ~373 bp insert / ~411 bp amplicon. Verified vs Parada 2016.

- **341F** `CCTACGGGNGGCWGCAG` (S-D-Bact-0341-b-S-17) + **805R** `GACTACHVGGGTATCTAATCC` (S-D-Bact-0785-a-A-21) — Klindworth 2013, exact match. ✓
- **27F** `AGAGTTTGATCMTGGCTCAG` — valid degenerate (M) form of Lane 1991 (original is CC). ✓
- **338R** `TGCTGCCTCCCGTAGGAGT` — correct 19-mer; the leading-T distinction from 18-mer 336R is accurately described. Covers V1-V2. ✓
- **534R** `ATTACCGCGGCTGCTGG` — HMP V1-V3 17-mer (519F revcomp). Covers V1-V3. ✓
- **1492R** `TACGGYTACCTTGTTACGACTT` — the widely-cited Y-degenerate 22-mer. ✓
- **944R** `GAATTAAACCACATGCTC` — sequence and E. coli position 944 confirmed. ✓
- All IUPAC codes (Y=C/T, M=A/C, R=A/G, W=A/T, N=ACGT, V=A/C/G, H=A/C/T) used correctly throughout.
- Amplicon sizes (~1500, 330, 525, 465, 290, 410, 430) are consistent with the coordinate spans.

# Adversarial Review: Self-Hit Confound & Accuracy/Gene-Capture Metrics

## Verdict
The two-branch include/exclude-self design is **directionally correct but not sufficient as specified.** The core flaw is that the proposed self-exclusion filter is built on a false premise about the reference DB's structure, and as a result it **systematically fails to exclude self in exactly the cases that matter most** — leaving the "honest" exclude-self metric still inflated, in a way that is invisible in the output. Several secondary issues compound this. Details and fixes below, grounded in the actual code/data.

---

## FINDING 1 (critical, invalidates the exclude-self filter as written): the reference DB is md5-deduplicated to ONE representative genome_id per sequence — so md5-identical self-copies in *other* genomes are not in the hits to be excluded, and the *source's own* operons may not be self-recoverable by genome_id either.

The design assumes hits contain multiple genome_ids that share the source's 16S md5, and that filter condition (2) (`h["md5"] == src_md5`) "drops *other* genome_ids that happen to share the identical 16S." **This cannot happen.** Verified:

- `edlib_biopython_hits.py:261-292`: references are the **deduplicated unique sequences** from `16S_md5_seq.json` (`md5 → seq`), and each md5 is mapped back to **exactly one** representative header via `16S_md5_ID.json` (`md5 → single header string`, confirmed: values are `str`, not lists). `parse_header` yields one `(organism, genome_id, taxon_id)` per md5.
- Measured: **460,117 unique md5 → 315,050 distinct representative genome_ids.** The same 16S sequence shared across many genomes collapses to **one** representative in hit space. A single genome_id represents up to **267** distinct md5s.

Consequences, both bad:

**(a) Filter condition (2) is nearly inert.** Within a single ASV's top-20, every hit already has a distinct md5 (identical-md5 references collapse to one entry before ranking). So `h["md5"] in src_md5_set` can only fire on the *source's own* operon copies — which are *already* a strict subset of what condition (1) catches by genome_id. The advertised purpose ("drop other genomes with identical 16S") is structurally impossible because those other genomes were never surfaced as separate hits. The design's headline justification for condition (2) is wrong.

**(b) The real leak is the inverse, and neither condition catches it.** If the source genome's 16S md5 is *represented in the DB by a different genome* (because dedup picked another genome as the representative for that md5), then:
- The amplicon will hit that representative at ~100% identity.
- `h["genome_id"] != src_genome_id` (condition 1 misses it).
- `h["md5"] == src_md5` — but only *if* the source's amplicon's md5 equals the full-length source md5. **It does not**, because the hit's `md5` is the *full-length reference* md5, while the amplicon was cut from a sub-region. The `src_md5` the design stores is "the md5 of the source genome's full-length 16S" — so `h["md5"] == src_md5` compares a full-length ref md5 to a full-length source md5. That *can* match (if the source's full-length 16S is byte-identical to the representative's), but it is fragile and not what the prose claims.

The net: a species-tier ASV whose source 16S is identical to some *other* genome's 16S still gets a ~100% non-self hit that is biologically self (same sequence, same or sister organism), and the exclude-self metric counts it as a legitimate generalization success. With **2,094 of 3,950 ASVs at species tier**, this is not a tail case.

**Fix.** Define self at the **md5 level against the true per-operon ground truth**, not against the deduped representative:
1. Build the authoritative `genome_id → {operon md5s}` and `md5 → {all genome_ids, all taxon_ids}` maps from `16S_metadata.json` (per-operon: `genome_id`, `taxon_id`, `na_sequence_md5`), **once**, cached to disk (the full parse is ~25+ min and 3.4GB RSS — do it once, persist a slim `{md5: [genome_ids]}` / `{genome_id: [md5s]}` pickle/json, never re-parse).
2. A hit is **self/identical-sequence** iff the hit's `md5` is in the set of md5s that the **source genome's operons** produce, OR the hit's representative `genome_id` is the source, OR the hit's `md5` is one whose `md5→genome_ids` set contains the source. Exclude on the *sequence identity of the operon*, computed against the **amplicon-region md5**, not the full-length md5 — because two genomes can share a V4–V5 insert while differing elsewhere in 16S.
3. Add a **near-identical** exclusion tier (see Finding 3) — exact md5 is not enough.

---

## FINDING 2 (critical): provenance md5 is the wrong md5 — full-length, not amplicon-region.

The design stores `src_md5 = md5 of the source genome's full-length 16S`. But the confound is created by the **amplicon region**, and the reference DB hits are full-length references aligned locally. Two distinct issues:

- The hit's `md5` field is the **full-length reference** md5 (`ref_seq_len: 1490` in the sample), not the amplicon's md5. So matching `h["md5"]` against any amplicon-derived hash is a category error; matching it against the full-length source md5 only works when full-length sequences are byte-identical.
- **Region collisions are the actual leak.** Many genomes that differ across the full 16S are **identical within V4–V5** (conserved-flanked hypervariable region). Those produce byte-identical amplicons but different full-length md5s, so condition (2) never fires, yet they are effectively self at the region level — which is precisely what a *hypervariable-region* validation study is trying to measure honestly.

**Fix.** Compute and store **three** md5s per amplicon in provenance: `src_genome_id`, `src_fulllen_md5_set` (all operon full-length md5s of the source), and `src_amplicon_md5` (md5 of the extracted insert itself). For exclusion, the decisive test is sequence identity at the **region** level: drop any hit whose reference, restricted to the aligned region, is identical (or ≥ near-identity threshold) to the amplicon. Since hits don't carry the reference's region-restricted md5, the robust implementation is: precompute, per region, the set of reference md5s whose **in-silico-PCR amplicon for that region** equals the source amplicon (you already run in-silico PCR over the whole DB to build the combined FASTA — reuse that to build an `amplicon_md5 → {ref genome_ids/ref full md5s}` index for free), and exclude hits whose reference falls in that set.

---

## FINDING 3 (high): exact-equality exclusion misses near-identical copies — the explicit concern in the prompt, and it is real.

Exact md5/genome_id equality does **not** catch:
- **Sister strains / same species, ≥99% but not 100% identical 16S** — these dominate species-tier hits and inflate accuracy nearly as much as exact self.
- **Different assembly of the same organism** (`taxon_id` equal, genome_id different). The accuracy design *does* define `hit_same_taxon` but only reports it; it is **not** wired into the default exclude-self filter (`mode="genome"`). For an honest generalization number you must also offer `mode="taxon"` and, more importantly, an **identity-threshold** exclusion.

**Fix.** Make exclusion a configurable cascade, report **all** levels side-by-side so the reader sees the leakage gradient:
1. `exact_self` — source genome_id or source operon md5 (Findings 1–2 corrected).
2. `same_taxon` — `hit.taxon_id == src_taxon_id` (other assemblies of the same organism).
3. `near_identical` — hit identity ≥ τ (e.g. ≥ 0.995 or ≥ species threshold 0.987) regardless of id/md5. This is the only filter that captures "the answer was effectively in the DB under a different accession."
The headline honest number should be the **strictest** (`near_identical`) variant, with the others reported as a leakage ladder. Excluding only exact genome_id (the current default `mode="genome"`) is the *weakest* and most inflated of the set.

---

## FINDING 4 (correct, keep it): re-running selection on filtered hits IS valid and necessary — but the filter script has two bugs.

Re-running `select_representatives` on a filtered `top20` is sound: it is a **pure function of one `asv_record`** (verified — reads `asv_record["best_identity"]` and `asv_record["top20"]`, no global state, no re-alignment), so the in-memory re-run is exact and cheap. The design correctly identifies that `best_identity` drives `_tier` (`select_references.py:118-125, 202, 255`) and **must** be recomputed, else the excluded-self run is still tiered on the self-hit's ~100% identity. Good catch. **But:**

- **Bug A — empty-survivor abort.** The standalone `filter_self_hits.py` sets `best_identity = None` when `kept` is empty. `select_representatives` then computes `_tier(None, k)` → `None >= 0.987` raises `TypeError`, crashing the whole run on the first all-self ASV. The accuracy design's `exclude_self()` correctly uses `0.0`; the pipeline design's script uses `None`. Use `0.0` (→ tier `below` → clean abstain) and reconcile the two scripts — they disagree.
- **Bug B — the filter script is redundant and risks divergence.** You have *two* self-exclusion implementations (the standalone JSON-rewriting `filter_self_hits.py` in the pipeline design, and the in-memory `exclude_self()` in the accuracy design). They use different match logic (`md5` set membership vs `mode`), different `best_identity` fallbacks, and the JSON-rewriter also mutates `best_align_score` which `select_representatives` never reads (`align_score` is read per-hit from `top20`, never `best_align_score`). **Drop the JSON-rewriting filter entirely**; keep the single in-memory `exclude_self(asv_record, ...) → select_representatives(...)` path. One code path, no on-disk intermediate that can desync.

---

## FINDING 5 (high): the accuracy "truth" can be circular / self-fulfilling when the source IS the representative.

`truth = lineage_for(int(src_genome_id.split('.')[0]))` and `predicted = lineage_for(hit.taxon_id)`, both via the same taxopy path — the comparability rule is correct (verified: `lineage_for` at `edlib_biopython_hits.py:268-283` builds `Kingdom = superkingdom or kingdom or domain`, and the sample hit shows `Kingdom: "Pseudomonadati"`, so truth/pred align bit-for-bit). **However**, when the source genome is itself the md5-representative (Finding 1), the *predicted* taxon_id under include-self is literally the *source* taxon_id, so every rank trivially matches — that is the leakage the study wants to quantify, fine. The subtle trap: even under exclude-self, if a *sister* genome shares the source's exact taxon_id (common — many assemblies per taxon), the "different" prediction has identical lineage and scores 100% correct at every rank. That is not generalization; it is the same organism. Finding 3's `same_taxon` exclusion is therefore **mandatory** for the accuracy metric, not optional.

---

## FINDING 6 (medium): gene-capture `exclude_source` removes only the source genome_id — same blind spot, and "source_only → recall 0" mislabels near-identical surrogates.

The gene-capture design's `exclude_source` (`R_eff = R \ {g*}`) inherits Finding 1's blind spot: if a near-identical sister was selected, recall stays ~1.0 and is reported as honest generalization. Worse, the `source_only` outcome (recall forced to 0 when g* was the only rep) will **under-report** capture in the very cases where a perfect surrogate exists, because the surrogate is the *source under a different accession* that `exclude_source` did not remove — so you get an artificially bimodal recall distribution (0.0 from `source_only`, ~1.0 from undetected-self), neither of which is the real generalization curve.

**Fixes:**
- Exclude at the **organism** level (`taxon_id == src_taxon_id`) and optionally the near-identity level, not just `genome_id == g*`, for the headline recall.
- The recall-vs-identity curve is the right instrument — but **bin by the identity of the *best non-self* hit**, after the corrected exclusion, so the x-axis is "distance to nearest genuinely-different reference." As currently specified it bins by `best_identity`, which under include-self is ~1.0 for almost everything (self) and tells you nothing.
- One real bug: `precision = i/p` with `p = |⋃ PGF(reps)|` is **monotonically gameable downward** but the design's claim that "recall alone is gameable by selecting more genomes" is the right guard — keep F1/Jaccard. However `truth_empty` (62/7395 ≈ 0.8%) and `pgfam_missing` must be **excluded from denominators**, which the design does correctly; just ensure the union `P` over reps with one `pgfam_missing` rep is flagged `pgfam_missing` for the *whole cell*, not silently treated as a smaller `P` (which would inflate precision). The spec is ambiguous here — make a missing rep poison the cell.

---

## FINDING 7 (medium): "deepest contiguous correct rank" silently rewards under-resolution; and abstention accounting can inflate apparent accuracy.

Two metric-inflation vectors in the accuracy design:

- **Abstention as free pass.** `abstained` ⇒ all ranks `None` ⇒ excluded from the %-correct denominator (`agg_rank` filters `None`). A pipeline that abstains on every hard case posts high "%correct" on a shrinking denominator. The design does include `coverage[rank]` — **good** — but the headline must be reported as the **pair** `(correct, coverage)` and ideally a single **coverage-penalized** score (e.g. correct×coverage, or count abstentions-on-confident-ASVs as errors). Otherwise "98% correct at Genus" over 20% coverage looks like success. The 139 `below`-tier ASVs abstain legitimately; but exclude-self will *push more ASVs below threshold* (their top hit was self at ~1.0), so the exclude-self denominator shrinks selectively toward easy cases — a structural inflation of the very metric meant to be honest. **Report exclude-self accuracy with the include-self denominator as the base** (abstentions counted as no-call against the full set), so the include→exclude drop reflects reality.
- **`overconfident` bucket.** Correctly separated (pred resolves deeper than truth defines) — keep it, and make sure it never counts as `True`. The `rank_correct` helper returns `None` when `truth_v` is falsy, which handles it. Good.

---

## FINDING 8 (low, but fix before running): operational/structural issues.

- **Amplicon key collisions.** `build_combined_fasta.py` proposes hashing the insert to a stable key. Identical inserts across genomes (conserved regions) collide to one key → provenance becomes ambiguous (which source genome?). The existing `insilico_pcr.py run_panel` already emits `{genome_id}__{region}` keys (`insilico_pcr.py:269`) which are **unique and carry provenance natively** — use the existing panel mode and skip the bespoke `build_combined_fasta.py` entirely. This also fixes the dedup-speedup tension: if you dedup identical inserts for alignment speed, you *lose* per-source provenance unless you keep the full `amplicon_md5 → [genome_id__region, ...]` fan-out map. The panel-mode keys give you that for free.
- **`load_asvs` truncates headers at first whitespace** (`edlib_biopython_hits.py:88`: `line[1:].split()[0]`). The design's sidecar-metadata-in-header convention (`src_genome_id=... src_md5=...`) is therefore *ignored by the aligner* — correct as the design notes — but it also means the **amplicon key the aligner emits is the pre-whitespace token**, so your provenance JSON must key on that exact token. With panel-mode `{gid}__{region}` keys (no whitespace) this is clean; with the proposed `>{ampliconKey} src_...` it works only because the key is first. Fine, but fragile — prefer panel keys.
- **`gpu-cand 100` vs `k2 20`:** the design discusses `--gpu-cand 100` for the GPU path; the emitted record is still `top20`. Confirm the GPU `align_hits.py` actually writes 20 (verified: GPU output has exactly 20 hits/ASV). If only 20 survive to disk, the self-filter can drop *all* of an ASV's non-self hits when self + sisters occupy the top 20 — leaving an empty `top20` and forcing abstention. **Record `n_removed_self` and how many ASVs become empty post-filter**; a high rate means top-20 is too shallow to support exclude-self and you need the top-500 hits (`asv_top500_alignment_hits_gpu.json` exists, 1.1GB) as the substrate for the exclude-self branch.

---

## Summary of required fixes (priority order)
1. **Redefine "self" against per-operon ground truth + region-level sequence identity** (`16S_metadata.json`-derived `md5↔genome` maps, cached once), not against the deduped representative or the full-length md5. (Findings 1, 2)
2. **Add `same_taxon` and `near_identical` (identity-threshold) exclusion tiers; report the leakage ladder; make the strictest the headline.** (Findings 3, 5, 6)
3. **Drop the JSON-rewriting `filter_self_hits.py`; keep one in-memory `exclude_self → select_representatives` path; use `best_identity=0.0` (not `None`) for empty survivors.** (Finding 4)
4. **Report `(correct, coverage)` pairs and compute exclude-self accuracy against the include-self (full) denominator** so abstention-shift can't inflate the honest number. (Finding 7)
5. **Use existing `insilico_pcr.py run_panel` (`{gid}__{region}` keys) instead of bespoke glue; carry `amplicon_md5 → [source...]` fan-out for region-collision detection and any insert dedup.** (Finding 8)
6. **Audit empties: log `n_removed_self`, post-filter empty-`top20` rate; if high, base exclude-self on top-500 hits, not top-20.** (Finding 8)

The include-self branch is fine as-is (it is an explicit upper bound). The exclude-self branch and every "honest generalization" number derived from it are **not trustworthy until fixes 1–3 land**, because as specified they leave region-level and same-organism self-leakage in the data while presenting it as out-of-sample.

**Relevant files:** `/home/freiburger/Documents/prFBA/select_references.py` (`select_representatives` pure-function re-run entry; reads `best_identity`+`top20`), `/home/freiburger/Documents/prFBA/edlib_biopython_hits.py:261-292` (md5→single-representative dedup, the root of Finding 1; `lineage_for` 268-283), `/home/freiburger/Documents/prFBA/insilico_pcr.py:236-310` (`run_panel`, `{gid}__{region}` keys — use instead of bespoke glue), `/home/freiburger/Documents/codiffusion_bioreactor/model_inputs/16S_md5_ID.json` (one header per md5 — proves the dedup), `/home/freiburger/Documents/codiffusion_bioreactor/model_inputs/16S_metadata.json` (authoritative per-operon `genome_id`/`taxon_id`/`na_sequence_md5` for the corrected self map), `/home/freiburger/Documents/EmilyKin/bvbrc_alignment_hits/asv_top20_alignment_hits_gpu.json` (hit schema; 20 hits/ASV).

# Parallelization + COST model sanity-check — VERDICT

Anchored to the **measured prior production run** (`/home/freiburger/Documents/EmilyKin/bvbrc_alignment_hits/run_stats.json`: 3,950 ASVs × 459,301 refs, k1=500, k2=20, 60 workers) and `gpu_align_stats.json` (57.3 GCUPS, exact-match-verified). Hardware confirmed: 64 cores, RTX 5070 Ti 15.7 GB free, 188 GB RAM.

## Bottom line
**Feasible in one run.** End-to-end ~**5.0 wall-hr at N=80k** (~2.6 hr at N=40k), **edlib-prefilter-bound** exactly as the design claims — but the design's GPU-memory worry is a non-issue, the BV-BRC host is wrong, and one parallelization defect in the GPU path materially changes throughput. No chunking required for the aligner. Details below.

## Stage-by-stage, corrected against the measured anchor

| Stage | Measured/derived basis | N=80k | N=40k |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. edlib top-500 prefilter (CPU) | **12.27 cpu-s/q measured** (48,472.5 cpu-s / 3,950), 59.5× effective speedup on 60 workers (measured) | **~4.6 wall-hr** | **~2.3 wall-hr** |
| 2. GPU SW of N×500 pairs | 57.3 GCUPS floor, qlen≈400 × reflen≈1500 | **~7 min** (40M pairs, 24 Tcells, 419 s) | ~3.5 min |
| 3. Biopython rescore (gpu_cand=100) | bio measured 2.47 cpu-s/q at depth-500 → scale ×100/500 | **~11 min** | ~5.5 min |
| enrichment (taxopy, single proc) | cached lineage, dominated by md5→header load | few min | few min |
| **Align total** | | **≈ 5.0 wall-hr** | **≈ 2.6 wall-hr** |

The design's headline (~4.8 hr / ~2.4 hr, prefilter-bound) is **correct to within ~5%**. The 12 cpu-s/q figure is real, not assumed.

## What the design got WRONG (fix before running)

1. **GPU memory framing is backwards — the "40M pairs in 16 GB" worry doesn't exist.** I measured the real device footprint: **~0.6 GB peak** (ref_codes uint8 = 500 MB, not 700 MB; ref_off 1.8 MB; qbuf 32 MB; one 4M-pair batch's qi+rj+out int32 = 48 MB). The 40M scores never co-reside on-device — `run_gpu` loops `pairs_batch=4_000_000` and copies each batch's int32 scores back to host (`align_hits.py:173-175`). You could raise `pairs_batch` to 40M and still sit under 1 GB. The actual host-side cost is the `scores`/`qi`/`rj` numpy arrays (N×500 int32 ×3 = **0.5 GB at N=80k**) — trivial against 188 GB RAM. **GPU is not a constraint at any N.**

2. **Wrong BV-BRC host.** The design's PGFam URL uses `www.bvbrc.org/api/...`; the actual working code (`prefetch_gene_families.py:33`) uses **`https://www.bv-brc.org/api/genome_feature/`** (hyphenated). Use the hyphenated host or every fetch 404s.

3. **PGFam fetch is NOT 10k calls — it's ~4.5k, and it's gated, threaded, resumable.** `prefetch_gene_families.py` only fetches genome_ids that reach the marginal-gain stage (its docstring: "~4.5k of ~21.7k top-20 genome_ids, ~79% saving"). At the code's default `workers=12` with `limit(25000)` per query and 3× retry/backoff, this is **API-latency-bound, ~20-45 min**, not a rate-limit wall. BV-BRC's Solr API tolerates ~12 concurrent streams fine; don't raise workers past ~12-16 (server-side, not your cores, is the limiter). Run it as a **prewarm before selection**, exactly as the design says.

4. **One real parallelization defect in the GPU path.** `run_gpu` Stage 1 spawns its Pool with **`Pool(workers)` and no `initializer`** (`align_hits.py:149`), then Stage 3 spawns a *second* `Pool(workers, initializer=P.init_worker)`. Two consequences:
   - The edlib workers re-fork the parent **after** `P.REF_BLOB` (500 MB) is populated — fine on Linux copy-on-write, but the two sequential Pools mean you pay fork + 500 MB COW-touch twice. Minor (~seconds).
   - More importantly, Stages 1, 2, 3 are **strictly sequential** (edlib fully drains → GPU → rescore). During the ~7-min GPU stage and the md5→header enrichment, **all 60 CPU workers sit idle**, and during the 4.6-hr edlib stage the GPU sits idle. That's acceptable here (GPU stage is 2% of wall) but it means the "60 workers + GPU concurrently" mental model is wrong — they never overlap. No code change needed; just don't expect the GPU to hide any edlib cost.

## Concrete settings (verified against the actual argparse)

```
--workers 60        # matches measured 59.5x speedup; >60 gives diminishing returns, leave 4 cores for GPU host + I/O
--prefilter-k 500   # do NOT lower — gpu_vs_pipeline comparison in gpu_align.py checks for hits outside top-500
--k2 20
--gpu-cand 100      # default; rescore depth, drives Stage-3 cost linearly
--force-backend cuda
--min-ref-len 200   # matches the 459,301-ref measured baseline
```
GPU internals (`run_gpu` defaults) need **no tuning**: `pairs_batch=4_000_000` is already 10× under the memory ceiling. `MAXQ=600` in `gpu_align.py` safely covers V4-V5 (≤450 bp) — confirmed, but the `assert maxq <= MAXQ` will abort if you ever concatenate a region whose insert exceeds 600 bp, so bump MAXQ first if you add V1-V9-spanning regions.

## Is full 1e4 × N tractable in one run? YES — but DEDUP first (the single highest-leverage move)

The aligner handles N=80k in one process with no chunking (memory verified above). **But the binding 4.6-hr edlib cost scales linearly in N and is the only thing worth attacking.** `load_asvs` keys on the *header*, and the cost is per *unique insert*. Across ~10k genomes the conserved-flank V-region inserts are heavily redundant — **dedup identical amplicon inserts before alignment, align the unique set, then fan results back out via `amplicon_provenance.json`.** This is the right place to cut N by a large factor (often 2-5×), turning the 4.6 hr into 1-2 hr, and it's free (md5 of the insert is already your key). The exhaustive GPU alternative (skip prefilter) is **~73 hr at N=80k** by the same 57.3 GCUPS — so the top-500 prefilter is correctly ~15× better and must stay.

**Chunking is only needed if** you can't tolerate a single ~5-hr process for fault-tolerance — in which case split the combined FASTA into, say, 4×20k shards (each ~1.2 hr), run sequentially in the same tmux, and concatenate the per-shard `asv_top20_alignment_hits.json`. The 500 MB reference load is re-paid per shard (~30 s each), negligible. This is the only reason to chunk; throughput-wise one run is fine.

# Completeness critique: 16S hypervariable-region validation design

I verified the design against the actual code/data before critiquing. Key confirmations: `make_extractor` in `/home/freiburger/Documents/prFBA/insilico_pcr.py:163` matches FWD on sense + REVC of REV on sense (so "both strands" is a misnomer — see G1); the panel hard-codes bacterial-only primers; `concordance_by_rank.json` reports no CIs and no per-region split; and critically, `gene_union` in the manifest stores **only counts, no gene-ID sets** (`gene_union has ID lists? False`), and there are **50 archaeal synthetic genomes** plus 4,964 archaea in the selection pool. Several proposed metrics are not computable as specified.

## CRITICAL BLOCKERS (the design as written cannot produce its headline figures)

**C1 — The gene-capture recall/precision/F1 metric is uncomputable from the stated data.** FIGURES F4/F5b/F8/F9/F12 all consume `gene_capture_long.csv` with `recall = genes recovered / genes in gold`. But the manifest's `gene_union` block stores only integer counts (`n_functions_union`, `n_core`, `n_shared`, `n_accessory`) — **no PGFam/gene-ID set**. You cannot compute set recall/precision from two cardinalities; |A∩B| is unknown. Fix: change the gene-union builder to persist the actual `pgfam_id` set per synthetic genome (e.g., `gene_union.pgfam_ids: [...]`), then recall = |region_set ∩ gold_set| / |gold_set|. Without this, every PR-space figure (F4, F8) and both correlation figures (F9, F12) are vapor. This is the single largest gap.

**C2 — Archaea coverage is unaddressed in selection AND silently biases the region panel.** The SELECTION pool is 4,964 archaea / 135,948 bacteria, and there are 50 archaeal synthetic genomes in the actual study. But the REGION panel's primers are **bacterial-domain primers**: 27F (`AGAGTTTGATCMTGGCTCAG`), 338R, 534R, 341F, 806R-Apprill, 1100F. Direct answer to the posed question: **no, these bacterial primers do not reliably amplify archaea** — 27F has well-known archaeal mismatches (the canonical full-length control will drop most archaea), 341F/805R V3-V4 is documented to be weak/biased for archaea (the panel notes even say "weaker for some archaea"), and 1100F is a bacterial-lineage primer. The only genuinely cross-domain pairs are 515F-Parada/926R and 515F/806R. **Consequence:** "extract_rate" and every accuracy/gene-capture number for archaea will collapse to near-zero in 6 of 8 core regions, and this will masquerade as "region is inaccurate" when it is actually "primer doesn't bind." Concrete additions:
  - Add a `domain` column to `region_meta.csv` and **stratify every figure by Bacteria/Archaea**, or explicitly scope the study to Bacteria and document the exclusion.
  - Add per-region **archaeal extract_rate** as a first-class reported number (it directly answers "does this primer amplify archaea").
  - In SELECTION, the √-flattening already over-weights the small archaeal pool — but if 6/8 regions can't amplify them, those archaeal slots are wasted budget. Either add archaeal primer variants (e.g., 515F-Arch/Arch806R, or the SSU_Euk/Arch sets) or down-scope.

**C3 — Selection over-counts available species; the "36,419 species ceiling" is the wrong denominator for the actual study.** The real study has **3,950 ASVs** (`findings_stats.json`), of which only 3,724 produced synthetic genomes and **2,094 are species-tier, 1,136 genus-tier, 581 family-tier, 139 below** (verified). The 10k deterministic selection of *reference* genomes is a separate artifact from the 3,950 ASVs the figures actually evaluate. The design never reconciles these two populations. The figures' `asv` axis is the 3,950 community ASVs, but the selection deliverable produces 10,000 reference genomes — **nowhere is it stated how the 10k selection feeds the region-matched reference store** that ASVs are hit against. State the join explicitly, or the selection is an orphan.

## REGIONS / PRIMERS

**R1 — V7-V9 and V6-V8 are the identical primer pair (1100F/1492R) emitting byte-identical amplicons.** Confirmed in `REGION_PANEL`: both use `fwd:YAACGAGCGCAACCC / rev:1492R / lo:350 / hi:430`. They will produce the same FASTA records and therefore **the same accuracy and gene-capture numbers** — two figure rows that are guaranteed duplicates. Either drop one, or actually differentiate by trimming reads to distinct V7-V9 vs V6-V8 windows post-extraction (the design hand-waves "depends on read length and trimming" but no trimming step exists). As implemented they are not two regions.

**R2 — No "primer fails to amplify" / selection-bias analysis, despite the question explicitly asking.** The panel reports hit-rate only on a 200-genome convenience sample (194-200/200). There is no figure or table for **which taxa systematically fail to amplify per region** — yet `make_extractor` returns `None` (silent skip) on non-amplification. This is a confound: a region with low concordance might simply be dropping hard taxa (survivorship bias — only easy-to-amplify genomes reach the accuracy computation). Concrete additions:
  - A **per-region, per-phylum amplification-failure table** (`n_input, n_amplified, fail_rate` by phylum) — this is the missing "selection bias" figure the prompt asks for.
  - Report accuracy on a **fixed common denominator** (genomes that amplify in *all* regions) as a sensitivity analysis, so region A isn't credited for accuracy on an easier subset than region B.
  - The 200-genome bound-tuning sample is too small and non-random to set production `lo/hi` insert bounds; re-tune on a stratified-by-phylum sample of ≥5,000 and report the per-region p1/p99 you actually observed.

**R3 — Ties/ambiguity at short regions is named in the prompt but absent from the design.** Short amplicons (V4 ~250 bp, V1-V2 ~330 bp) produce many references at cosine ≈ 1.0 (the report already notes V-regions tie near cosine 1.0, which is why species rank is dropped). The top-20 hit logic has **no tie-handling policy**: if 50 references tie at cosine 1.0, top-20 is an arbitrary truncation and `any_top20_concordance` becomes a function of the arbitrary sort order among ties. Add: (a) report **number of references within ε of best cosine** per ASV×region as an ambiguity metric, and (b) make the top-k tie cutoff deterministic and document it, and (c) add an "ambiguity-adjusted" concordance (concordant if the correct name is anywhere in the full tie cluster, not just the truncated 20).

## EXTRACTION

**G1 — "Both strands" is not handled; reverse-strand and partial 16S genes are missed.** `make_extractor` only searches FWD-then-REVC on the *given* sense strand (confirmed at line 163-176). BV-BRC 16S genes extracted on the minus strand, or sequences deposited 3'→5', will silently fail to amplify and be dropped — another invisible selection bias. Add a reverse-complement pass: if `extract(seq)` is None, try `extract(revcomp(seq))`. Also handle genes where the forward primer site is truncated (partial 16S): currently a missing 27F site drops the whole genome from the full-length control even if V4-V5 is intact.

**G2 — `emax=3` fuzzy fallback is applied independently to each primer with no mismatch accounting in output.** A genome amplified only via 3+3 = 6 total mismatches is biologically a non-amplifier in a real PCR, yet counts identically to a perfect match. Record per-amplicon `fwd_edits, rev_edits` in the stats and offer a strict mode; otherwise lenient regions look artificially universal. Also: `regex` `{e<=3}` allows indels that can shift the insert frame — verify the emitted amplicon boundaries on a few fuzzy hits.

## ACCURACY / STATISTICAL REPORTING

**A1 — No confidence intervals or per-region n anywhere.** `concordance_by_rank.json` gives point estimates only. Every concordance and gene-capture number is a proportion over a finite (and region-varying) n — F1/F2/F4/F6/F10 must carry **Wilson 95% CIs** (the design only adds CIs to F6). Critically, `n_evaluable` **differs across regions** (because amplification failure differs), so cross-region comparisons are between different denominators — state n per cell and test differences with a paired McNemar test on the common-amplified ASV subset, not eyeballed heatmap deltas.

**A2 — Leave-one-out / self-match contamination is acknowledged (F11) but not enforced in the core pipeline.** The headline numbers (`genus any20 = 0.66`) almost certainly include each ASV's own genome as a top hit. F11 computes the delta, but the **primary** accuracy figures (F1, F2, F10) should be reported exclude-self by default, with include-self as the inflation check — otherwise the headline grid is optimistically biased and region differences may be dominated by self-match availability rather than discriminating power.

**A3 — Reproducibility gap in the heavy precompute.** The SELECTION core is rigorously deterministic (seed 1729, sorted iteration). But the embedding/hit pipeline is not addressed: NT-v2 GPU embedding + cosine top-k can be **non-deterministic** (CUDA non-determinism, ties). Pin `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`, fix `PYTHONHASHSEED`, sort ties deterministically in top-k, and record the GPU/driver/library versions in `region_meta.csv`. Otherwise "same inputs → same figures" holds only for selection, not for the numbers in the figures.

## FIGURES — do they answer "accuracy and % gene capture by region"?

**F-accuracy:** Yes, F1/F2/F3/F10 cover accuracy well once CIs (A1) and exclude-self (A2) are added.

**F-gene-capture:** **No, not as specified** — blocked by C1 (no gene-ID sets to compute recall/precision). Additionally:
- **The gene-capture metric is conceptually circular.** "Gold = full-16S reference set's gene union" assumes the full-16S resolution is correct, but the study's own thesis is that names are unreliable. If the full-16S gold set is itself mis-resolved, recall against it measures agreement-with-a-longer-amplicon, not truth. State this is **relative** capture (vs full-length), not absolute, and label axes accordingly.
- **% gene capture is never plotted as a simple per-region percentage.** The prompt asks for "percent gene capture by region." F4 plots recall/precision/F1 violins, but there is no clean **bar of mean % gene captured per region with CI** — the most direct answer to the literal question. Add it.
- **No region × tier interaction.** Gene-capture is dominated by tier (`species` synthetic genomes have tight unions; `family`-tier are huge — the Stappiaceae example has n_accessory=7453). 2,094 species vs 581 family-tier means gene-capture differences across regions may be a tier-mix artifact. Facet F4/F8 by `tier`, or report tier-stratified.

**F-missing entirely:**
- **Amplification-rate figure** (R2) — the selection-bias answer.
- **Per-region ambiguity / tie-cluster-size figure** (R3).
- **Archaea vs bacteria split** on F1/F4/F10 (C2).
- **F9 as specified plots jittered 0/1 concordance vs F1** — replace x with continuous `best_cosine` (the design even notes this is cleaner) and report Spearman with CI; a Spearman on a binary x is just a rank-biserial and will mislead.
